findings.headline: Acquiring an established star (origin-team YTD WAR ≥ 2.5) is the only truly dominant archetype: highest mean AND lowest whiff AND a deeply positive floor.
findings.gm_action: If you cannot whiff, pay up for a player already producing 2.5+ WAR for his current club. P25 outcome is still +$8.5M. Replicates on war_delta (mean +3.74, whiff 0.19) and surplus_wins (mean +3.40). Thin sample (n=52); directional.
findings.novelty: No published cut showed the star tier is the only bucket that simultaneously lifts mean and raises the downside floor above zero — stochastic dominance for a risk-averse buyer.

findings.headline: Pure-pitcher acquisitions are systematically higher-variance and whiff more than pure-hitter acquisitions on EVERY outcome metric.
findings.gm_action: A pitcher loses money 38% of the time vs 27% for a hitter, P25 floor 5x worse. The higher pitcher mean is paid entirely in tail risk. war_delta whiff 0.257 vs 0.173; surplus_wins 0.452 vs 0.309. Prefer the bat at equal projected value.
findings.novelty: First showing the acquisition-side pitcher-vs-hitter gap is a pure VARIANCE gap (means within $1.3M), not a mean gap.

findings.headline: Acquiring a player aged 30+ is the worst value trap: 42% whiff and the worst floor in the dataset, with no mean premium.
findings.gm_action: Near coin-flip whiff (42%) and deepest negative P25 (-$2.80M), yet mean barely above baseline. Buying downside with no EV compensation. surplus_wins: 54% whiff, P25 -0.44 wins.
findings.novelty: Reframes age>=30 as a downside-tail/whiff problem, not a mean-decline problem — the mean barely moves; the floor collapses.

findings.headline: Young acquisitions (age < 24) are the best SAFE-FLOOR archetype at scale: lowest whiff (17.6%) of any large bucket, zero floor.
findings.gm_action: Deployable safe play at volume: whiff 17.6%, P25 floor $0. Best floor available at scale (star tier floor is better but only 52 comps). surplus_wins: whiff 0.180, P25 0.00, mean +1.00 wins.
findings.novelty: Youth's real edge is the FLOOR — it almost never loses money — not its (unremarkable) mean.

findings.headline: Variance is separable from the mean, and origin-team WAR is the dominant variance predictor.
findings.archetype_or_feature: |residual| regression after removing OLS mean effect
findings.gm_action: ~7% of absolute-residual variation is predictable independent of the mean. Dominant variance driver is origin_ytd_war (std-coef ~$3.28M, ~3x next, pct_pitchers ~$1.0M). Higher-WAR targets have higher EV AND wider spread; stars are 'safe' only because their mean clears zero.
findings.novelty: First explicit test that variance is modelable apart from the mean on this dataset; dev_fit_hitting (~$0.71M) is a secondary variance driver.

dead_ends: receiver_payroll_pct_of_cap: flat across quartiles (whiff 0.218-0.252). Big spenders do not whiff less.
receiver_contention_window_score: nearly flat (whiff 0.225-0.259); contender status does not move the floor.
receiver_acquired_avg_fv: too sparse on acquiring side for a credible variance cut.
receiver_acquired_milb_age_advantage: top bucket high mean ($9.3M) but elevated whiff (0.319) — mild trap; superseded by raw-age cut.
